name: Electric Bicycle
description: A pedaled vehicle with an electric motor of less than 750 watts, in one of three classes: class 1 and class 2 (throttle) stop at 20 mph, class 3 (pedal assist) at 28 mph.

restrictions.rule: Class 1 assists only while pedaling and stops at 20 mph; class 2 can propel it without pedaling and stops at 20 mph; class 3 assists only while pedaling and stops at 28 mph (New Hampshire RSA 259:27-a, from HB 148 (2019))
The motor must disengage when the brakes are applied (New Hampshire RSA 265:144-a)
Class 3 must have a speedometer showing its speed in miles per hour (New Hampshire RSA 265:144-a)
Riders of class 3 must be 16 or older; a younger passenger may ride on one designed to carry passengers (New Hampshire RSA 265:144-a)
Riders and passengers under 18 on a class 3 must wear a bicycle helmet meeting CPSC or ASTM standards (New Hampshire RSA 265:144-a)
Riders under 16 on any class must wear a helmet on a public way, under the bicycle helmet law
Carries no more people than it's designed and equipped for
Carries a permanent label stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage (New Hampshire RSA 265:144-a)
Must not be tampered with or modified to change its motor-powered speed or engagement unless the label is replaced to match (New Hampshire RSA 265:144-a)
Meets the CPSC's bicycle requirements (16 CFR part 1512) (New Hampshire RSA 265:144-a)
Has the rights and duties of a bicycle and is not a motor vehicle or an off highway recreational vehicle: no driver's license, registration, title, plate or insurance (New Hampshire RSA 265:144-a)
Class 1 and 2 may use bicycle and multi-use paths, but a city, town or state agency may ban them from a path it manages (New Hampshire RSA 265:144-a)
Class 3 is kept off bicycle and multi-use paths unless the path runs within or beside a roadway or the city, town or state agency over it allows it (New Hampshire RSA 265:144-a)
On a natural-surface trail designated nonmotorized, the agency that manages the trail decides whether it's allowed (New Hampshire RSA 265:144-a)
On state parks and forests, class 1 and 2 may use trails open to bicycles, class 3 only recreational roads, park roads and rail trails, all at 20 mph or less unless signed
